sections.title: Plant and flowers
sections.text: Red clover is a short-lived perennial or biennial herb, about 15–60 cm tall and 20–50 cm across. It has three leaflets, often marked with a pale chevron, and rounded heads of pink to purplish flowers.

sections.title: Edible parts
sections.text: Young leaves and flowering heads are eaten raw or cooked; the flower heads are also dried. North Carolina Extension notes that the flowers are not easily digested and advises against eating them during pregnancy or nursing. The plate’s upright stems and pink heads distinguish it from creeping white clover.
